sum_p: Southern Machinery (Shenzhen, founded 2011) builds customized feeders and nozzles that let odd-form insertion machines and SMT mounters pick parts standard feeders cannot present: SAF1001 axial tape, SRF1001 radial tape, STF1003 tube, SBF1001 vibratory bowl, SBF2002 belt, STP1001 tray, SJF1001 jumper wire, SRT7001 reel terminal, SSPC101 solder chip and SLF1001 label feeders, plus gripper and custom vacuum nozzles. The quick-match table maps 76 real component lines to those models by packaging, pitch and body size.

why_h2: The part is ready for automation. Its packaging is not.
why_lead: On most THT boards the radial and axial parts are already machine-inserted. What is left on the manual line is a list of odd shapes, each arriving in a different box.
w1t: Six packaging types on one board
w1d: Headers in bags, a relay in a tube, a transformer in a tray, Y-capacitors on ammo tape. A standard feeder bank expects one format, so the rest goes to hands.
w2t: Pitch that does not match the feeder
w2d: An X2 capacitor at 22.5 mm lead pitch is wider than a standard radial feeder's 15 mm body limit. The evaluation sheets mark exactly these lines as needing a custom feeder.
w3d: Open-frame headers, stacked USB and audio jacks have no flat top for a vacuum cup. Without a gripper nozzle shaped for the body, the head drops or tilts the part.
w4d: Half the lines on a typical odd-form list carry a description and a packaging code but no dimensions. Feeder selection stalls until someone measures the sample.
w5d: Trimmers, LEDs and buzzers in bulk must reach the pick point in one attitude. A bowl or belt feeder has to sort direction before the head arrives.
w6t: Every machine brand has its own rail
w6d: The feeder must mount, signal and stay at a repeatable pick position on your machine, not on a demo bench.

mx_note: Mapping rules: packaging decides the feeder family; body size, pitch and lead diameter are checked against the Catalog V03 envelope of that model. 'Fits catalog' means the source evaluation passed and the part is inside the published envelope; it is not a guarantee for your exact part. 'Confirmed mapping' is a confirmed pairing with a feeder outside Catalog V03: the host machine's own 32 mm tape feeder or the S-MVF01. Part numbers, customer names and suppliers are withheld.

mx_chk_out: An envelope check is not a test. Orientation, lead stiffness and your machine's pick height decide the final answer.

mx_f_srf1001d: Feeds, forms, cuts and optionally bends (90°) radial parts from tape: electrolytic, Y- and square capacitors, terminals, springs, bent resistors. Outline 2×2×3 to 15×15×30 mm, lead core 0.3–1.0 mm, cut length 3–6 mm, tape hole pitch 12.7 or 15 mm (not interchangeable), ±0.2 mm, 1 s per cycle.
mx_f_saf1001d: Feeds taped resistors, triodes and jumper wires with U-shaping and lead trimming; material 3×3 to 6×20 mm, tape width 35, 64 or 92 mm (other widths built to order), ±0.3 mm, 0.8 s, optional paper tape return.
mx_f_stf1003d: Feeds tube-packed relays, terminals, transformers, square and round capacitors, DIPs and transistors; 3×3×3 to 25×25×25 mm, PVC or aluminium tubes 200–650 mm, several tubes stacked, ±0.5 mm, 0.8 s, dual channel on request.
mx_f_sbf1001d: Sorts, orients and feeds bulk electronic components, hardware, plastic parts and connectors; 3×3 to 50×50 mm, 10–300 g, polarity sorting and lead cutting as options, single or front-and-rear bowls, ±0.5 mm, 0.8 s.
mx_f_sbf2002d: Compact, quiet bulk feeder with material selection and NG return for connectors, buzzers, network ports, terminals and square capacitors; 3×3×3 to 20×20×20 mm, ±1 mm, 1.5–2 s. Not for easily deformed pins.
mx_f_stp1001d: Supplies tray parts such as transformers, relays, hardware, memory sockets and large capacitors; 3×3×3 to 50×50×50 mm, PET blister trays 150×150 to 200×300 mm, up to 40 trays, ±1 mm, 3 s per part.
mx_f_sjf1001d: Straightens, cuts, forms and feeds tinned copper wire Ø0.5–1.2 mm from the roll; pin span 6–40 mm, pin length 3–5 mm, 5-minute mould change, ≤1.5 s per piece, no compressed air.
mx_f_srt7001d: Cuts and feeds reel terminals (tab 6.35 × 0.81 mm, 10.21 mm above the PCB) for SMT/THT machines and automated lines; ±0.5 mm, 0.8 s, empty-reel alarm after 3 misses.
mx_f_sspc101d: Cuts and feeds solder sheet or wire from the coil, width 1–16 mm, thickness 0.1–1 mm; ±0.5 mm, 1.2 s, shortage alarm.
mx_f_slf1001d: Peels and presents labels, films, foam, adhesive, copper foil or steel sheet from the roll; liners under 60/80/100 mm, 0.05–0.08 mm thick, 3-inch core, ±0.2 mm X/Y.
mx_f_smvf01d: A separate model from the Catalog V03 SBF2002, with its own specification sheets, manual and videos, and its own component range. Bulk feeding: a motor-driven belt lifts loose parts to a selection track, rejected parts return on the belt, accepted parts reach the pick point by direct vibration, and a fibre-optic sensor confirms the part. IO communication or stand-alone. Component fit is confirmed per part with a sample.

npi_h2: Five steps from odd-form BOM to running feeder
npi_lead: The order an NPI engineer can follow for every odd-form line, so the feeder decision is made with data, not after the first failed trial.
n1d: Write down how each odd-form part actually arrives at your line, not how the datasheet says it can be ordered. Packaging decides the feeder family.
n1c1: Every odd-form line has a packaging code: bulk, tube, tray, radial tape, axial tape, embossed tape or coil.
n1c2: Lines with two possible packagings are flagged; ask purchasing which one is on the PO.
n1c3: For taped radial parts, the tape hole pitch (12.7 or 15 mm) is recorded.
n2d: Measure the real sample: body L × W × H, overall height above the board, lead pitch, lead count and lead diameter. These are the numbers the feeder envelope is checked against.
n2c1: Body L × W × H and overall height measured on the sample, in mm.
n2c2: Lead pitch, lead count and lead diameter recorded; any bent or kinked lead noted.
n2c3: Polarity mark and pick surface identified: flat top for vacuum, or a body that needs a gripper.
n3d: Use the quick-match table: packaging gives the family, dimensions check the envelope of the model. Parts outside the envelope go straight to the custom list.
n3c1: Each line mapped to a model (SRF1001, STF1003, SBF1001, SBF2002, STP1001 …) or to 'custom'.
n3c2: Nozzle type chosen per line: gripper or vacuum with a custom tip.
n3c3: Feeder slots counted against the space on your insertion machine.
n4t: Send samples or BOM for a free test
n4d: Send the list with photos, the dimensions and five to ten samples of every doubtful part, plus the exact insertion machine model and photos of its feeder rail.
n4c1: BOM with dimensions and packaging sent; part numbers may stay internal.
n4c2: Samples of every 'custom' or 'to be confirmed' line sent.
n4c3: Machine brand, model and feeder-rail photos sent.
n5d: Run the feeder on your machine with your parts, log feeding rate and stops, and compare the labour released with the cost of the feeder set.
n5c1: Trial run logged: parts fed, mis-picks, stops and their causes.
n5c2: Manual insertion hours released per month calculated (worksheet below).
n5c3: Spare parts, wear items and operator training agreed before the order.
fab_h2: Six technical advantages, each with a number behind it
fab_lead: Feature, what it does on the machine, and what it changes for your line.
fab1f: Ten catalog feeder models covering axial, radial, tube, bowl, belt, tray, jumper wire, reel terminal, solder chip and label supply, each a base for customization.
fab1a: Track, mould or tray is adapted to your part instead of forcing the part into a standard format.
fab1b: Lines that stayed manual because no OEM feeder fits can move onto the machine.
fab2f: Gripper nozzles with a fixed arm and a swing arm for odd shapes, special connectors and hybrid circuits; custom nozzles with interchangeable rubber tips for THT parts.
fab2a: The pick follows the body, so open headers, jacks and capacitors are held square through vision and insertion.
fab2b: Fewer drops and tilted inserts on exactly the parts that cause most manual rework.
fab3f: Every catalog model connects through an 8-core 16 mm aviation plug and runs with IO communication or on its own without communication.
fab3a: The feeder signals 'part ready' to the host, or runs stand-alone on a robot cell or non-standard machine.
fab3b: One feeder design serves odd-form inserters, SMT mounters and robot arms; the catalog lists installs on four machine brands.
fab4f: Release records in Catalog V03: 48 hours continuous ageing on every model, plus 500 to 1,000 consecutive feeds without abnormality (2 hours continuous feeding for the bowl).
fab4a: Feeding faults show up on the bench, not during your first production week.
fab4b: Commissioning time goes into your parts and program, not into debugging the feeder.
fab5f: Published feeding accuracy: ±0.2 mm radial and label, ±0.3 mm axial, ±0.5 mm tube, bowl, terminal and solder, ±1 mm tray and belt.
fab5a: You know which family can serve a tight pick position before you design the cell.
fab5b: Realistic expectations at NPI; tolerance questions are settled on paper.
fab6f: Send samples or a BOM with dimensions; Southern Machinery engineering checks each line against feeder envelopes and your machine before quoting.
fab6a: Doubtful parts are tested on a feeder, not guessed from a datasheet.
fab6b: You commit to a feeder set with a written per-line result: fits, needs customization, or not possible.

q1t: Which feeder do I need for an odd-form part?
q1a: Start from the packaging: bulk goes to the SBF1001 bowl or SBF2002 belt, tubes to STF1003, trays to STP1001, radial tape to SRF1001, axial tape to SAF1001, coils to SJF1001, SRT7001 or SSPC101. Then check body size, pitch and lead diameter against that model's envelope in the quick-match table. The S-MVF01 reciprocating belt feeder is a separate model from SBF2002, with its own sheet; bulk parts are matched to it per part.
q2t: Do Southern Machinery feeders work with my insertion machine or SMT mounter?
q2a: Every Catalog V03 model connects through an 8-core 16 mm aviation plug and runs with IO communication or stand-alone. The catalog shows installs on Panasonic CM602, JUKI, YAMAHA and Mirae odd-form machines; the exact mounting is confirmed from photos of your feeder rail.
q3t: What is the largest component a feeder can take?
q3a: Up to 50×50×50 mm on the STP1001 tray feeder and 50×50 mm on the SBF1001 bowl (10–300 g). Tube parts go up to 25 mm, belt-fed parts up to 20 mm and radial taped parts up to 15×15×30 mm; anything larger is a customized feeder.
q4t: My X2 capacitor has a 22.5 mm pitch. Can it be fed?
q4a: Not by the standard SRF1001, whose body envelope stops at 15 mm. Such lines are marked 'to be confirmed' in the table and handled as a customized radial feeder after a sample test.
q5t: When do I need a gripper nozzle instead of vacuum?
q5a: When the part has no flat, sealed top: open pin headers, wafers, many connectors and Y-capacitors. Gripper nozzles with a fixed and a swing arm hold the body; parts with a flat top, such as jacks or electrolytic capacitors, usually take a vacuum nozzle with a custom tip.
q6a: As published in Catalog V03: ±0.2 mm radial and label feeders, ±0.3 mm axial, ±0.5 mm tube, bowl, terminal and solder, ±1 mm tray and belt.
q7t: Is the feasibility test really free?
q7a: Yes. Send the BOM with dimensions and packaging, samples of doubtful parts and your machine model; you receive a written per-line result before any order.
q8a: Catalog V03 does not state one. Lead time is quoted per project after the sample test, because it depends on how much customization each line needs.
q9t: Can bulk parts with polarity be fed in the right direction?
q9a: Yes, when the polarity is physically recognizable. The SBF1001 bowl offers polarity sorting and lead cutting as options; the SBF2002 belt needs parts whose features can be told apart physically.
q10t: How are the feeders tested before shipment?
q10a: Each catalog model carries a 48-hour continuous ageing test and 500 to 1,000 consecutive feeds without abnormality; the bowl feeder is run for 2 hours of continuous feeding.
